results.finding_key: packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-signature.guard.ts::webhook signature header name/format is an unverified assumption; a mismatch silently 401s every event and `updatedat` never advances

verdict.reasoning: I verified the in-repo half: yorkie-signature.guard.ts:48-59 reads `req.header('x-signature-256')` and does a strict length+timingSafeEqual against `sha256=<hex>`, throwing 401 with no accept-path logging, and yorkie-signature.guard.spec.ts signs using the same convention as the code under test, so the suite cannot detect a wrong external contract — the claim is accurate about all of that, and about the consequence (silent 401s, updatedAt never advancing from edits). The decisive fact — Yorkie v0.7.12's actual header name — is not in this repository (the Go client is not vendored; only the PR's own docs/design/documents-last-modified.md:47 asserts it), so I could not check it with the tools available. My recollection of Yorkie's webhook client is that the header constant is the Yorkie-specific `X-Signature-Y256` rather than `X-Signature-256`, which would make this a real defect, but that is memory rather than verification, hence low confidence. Note the claim's casing worry is moot — Express's `req.header()` is case-insensitive — so only a literal name/prefix difference matters.

results.finding_key: packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-event.controller.spec.ts::test titled 'always answers ok so yorkie does not retry' only exercises the trivial early-return path

verdict.reasoning: Verified against the supplied sources: in `yorkie-event.controller.ts` the handler resolves `key = body.attributes?.key` → `undefined`, so `parsed` is `null` and it returns `{ ok: true }` at the `!parsed` guard — the spec case at `yorkie-event.controller.spec.ts:66` posts exactly `{ type: 'DocumentRootChanged' }` with no `attributes`, so it never reaches `touchUpdatedAt`. The controller also has no try/catch around `await this.documentService.touchUpdatedAt(...)`, and no spec case makes the mock reject, so the claimed "always 200, never retry" property is indeed untested for the failure path; the test's title over-promises relative to what it exercises. Note the other specs do drive the `touchUpdatedAt` path (with a resolving mock), so coverage of the happy path exists — the genuine gap is only the rejection case. Impact is limited: a 500 on a DB outage causes Yorkie to retry, which is arguably the desired behaviour rather than a data-correctness bug, so this is a test-naming/coverage gap rather than a functional defect.

results.finding_key: docs/tasks/active/20260710-docs-list-updatedat-webhook-todo.md::the originating task's verification criterion for an e2e test of the webhook path is not met

verdict.reasoning: The task file's Verification block (docs/tasks/active/20260710-docs-list-updatedat-webhook-todo.md, "## Verification": "e2e: signed webhook advances `updatedAt`; unsigned/bad-sig rejected") asserts e2e coverage, but the diff adds only three unit specs — yorkie-event.controller.spec.ts, yorkie-signature.guard.spec.ts, document.service.spec.ts — each constructing the class directly with a mocked DocumentService/PrismaService; no new file appears under packages/backend/test/, and the supplied directory listing of that folder at this commit (14 entries) contains no yorkie/webhook e2e spec. So nothing exercises the route through Nest's HTTP stack: the `bodyParser.json({ verify })` raw-body capture in packages/backend/src/main.ts (whose `req.url === '/internal/yorkie/events'` match is exactly the kind of wiring only an HTTP-level test catches), the guard registration in document.module.ts, and the monotonic `updateMany` SQL in touchUpdatedAt are all untested end to end. The Tasks section itself concedes "DB-backed e2e for the advance-only path deferred", which contradicts the Verification claim rather than satisfying it. Impact is limited to documentation accuracy plus a coverage gap on a security-relevant guard, not a user-visible defect.

results.finding_key: docs/design/documents-last-modified.md::new standalone top-level design doc instead of folding into the canonical backend doc, contrary to the repo's stated doc-filing policy

verdict.reasoning: The policy quote is verbatim accurate: docs/design/README.md's "Obsolete docs" section says the durable design "lives in its canonical subsystem doc above, regardless of whether it shipped as a single PR. Fold a single-PR note into the relevant doc as a concise subsection rather than keeping it as a standalone file." The diff instead adds a standalone docs/design/documents-last-modified.md plus a Common-section README row, and never touches docs/design/backend.md, whose Document ER entry still lists only id/title/authorID/createdAt and whose API reference has no /internal/yorkie/events endpoint — so backend.md's schema/API description is left divergent. Two caveats reduce weight: the Common section already contains many arguably single-feature standalone docs (comments-mentions.md, rest-api.md, context-menu.md), so the convention is loosely enforced in practice, and backend.md was already stale before this PR (it omits Document.workspaceId/type and the workspace-scoped routes), so this PR only adds one more divergence rather than newly invalidating it. Documentation-organization only; no user-facing or correctness impact.
